A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EntQuant work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity and accuracy evaluations, instruction-model benchmarks, inference measurements, and ablations, including Tables C.1–C.3 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sequence-length latency measurements in Figure 6 and per-layer weight analysis in Figure B.2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the optimization objective, channel scaling, quantization formats, and ANS decoding remain unchanged. The block-wise decoding procedure emphasized in v2 Section 2.2 was already documented in v1 Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets, language-model families, and accuracy tasks are retained. The added prefill study varies settings within existing inference evaluation. Healthcare, finance, and diffusion models receive additional discussion but are not newly evaluated.

E2.justification: The benchmark compression comparators remain unchanged. Appendix B.1 adds two analytical sparsity baselines, using uniform nonzero values and the original nonzero distribution, quantified in Table B.1 and compared against EntQuant in Figure B.2. These are analytical references, not newly benchmarked compression implementations.

E3.justification: Figure 6 adds a prefill-latency protocol for LLaMA-3.1 70B at batch size one with input lengths from 512 to 8192 tokens. Existing accuracy metrics, few-shot settings, precision configurations, and hardware descriptions are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused analyses of context-length-dependent latency, entropy reduction beyond sparsity alone, and per-layer entropy versus sparsity and reconstruction error. These supplement the retained super-weight, quantization-format, activation, and inference analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports per-setting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The aggregate statement of over 480 runs is unchanged; Figure B.2 shows variation across weight matrices, not uncertainty across repeated trials.

E6.justification: The 70B compression-time estimate changes from under 30 minutes to under 10 minutes in v1 Table 3a versus v2 Table 4a, without establishing a threefold implementation speedup. v2 adds memory-component estimates, latency-versus-length results, and layerwise and sparsity-reference findings. Existing accuracy tables and Appendix F measurements are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds a zero/nonzero mixture entropy calculation and two assumptions about the nonzero distribution, supporting the theoretical sparsity comparisons in Table B.1. The maximum-entropy bound and its derivation in Appendix B.2 already appeared in v1 and remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal data-free, approximately two-bit compression contribution is retained. The abstract and concluding remarks strengthen the compression-time bound from under 30 to under 10 minutes. The abstract removes 'the first framework,' although the discussion retains its first-method claim.

C2.justification: v2 explains nonzero-distribution reshaping beyond sparsity and amortization of decoding overhead over longer contexts. It cautions against attributing accuracy to individual-layer entropy, softens the compute-bound characterization, and expands discussion of inference optimization, non-LLM applicability, and safety implications.

D1.justification: New Table 2 itemizes memory components, including an approximately 0.8 GiB decompression buffer and KV-cache assumptions of batch size one, 4096 tokens, and 16-bit activations. The compression-time estimate is revised. Existing software, hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information are retained; block-wise implementation details are largely relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adopts Nagel et al.'s four-level quantization taxonomy and adds supporting literature on quantization, reasoning, and safety. It replaces the C4 and IFEval source citations with Raffel et al. and Zhou et al., respectively. The central positioning relative to entropy coding and fixed-width quantization remains intact.

P1.justification: Parts of the introduction and discussion are rewritten or expanded, and conflict-of-interest and substantive impact statements are added. Software/accessibility information and the block-wise decoder explanation move earlier. The overall section and appendix organization remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the memory table, Table B.1, the latency Figure 6, and Figure B.2. It adds a taxonomy-level column to Table 4a and changes palettes and bar outlines in existing plots. Other displays are retained with relocation and renumbering, including v1 Figure 6 becoming v2 Figure 7.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the memory breakdown, context-length latency study, and expanded Appendix B provide useful evidence about deployment costs and why compression exceeds sparsity alone. Clearer qualifications also improve interpretation. These are targeted gains to an already extensive study; the tighter runtime estimate does not itself demonstrate an implementation improvement.
